test_title: PYST 26: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 2 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

He brought these sweets __for you and I.__
solution:
The correct answer is** option 4, "for you and me."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The appropriate phrase to substitute is **"for you and me".**
 
• The reason is that **"me" **is the object of the preposition **"for." **
 
• In this sentence,** "me" **is in the objective case because it is the object of the preposition **"for."**
 
 
• Example: He gave the gift to my sister and **me**.
 
 
 
• Thus, an objective pronoun is needed.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *He brought these sweets __**for you and me**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Subjective pronouns** are used as the **subject **of a sentence. They are:

 
 
• I, You, He, She, It, We, They
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• **She **is going to the store.
 
• **We **are having a party tonight.
 
 
 
• **Objective pronouns** are used as the **object **of a sentence. They are:
 
• Me, You, Him, Her, It, Us, Them
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• He gave the book to **me**.
 
• She saw **him **at the park.
 
 
 
• Note that **"it"** is the same for both subjective and objective pronouns.
